title: Grade 4 CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION — 3.9 Nicodemus’ encounter with Jesus Christ

pages.lesson:
PAGE 1: Overview

OVERVIEW
========

John 3:1-5 tells how Nicodemus, a Pharisee and a member of the Jewish ruling council, came to Jesus at night. Jesus told him that no one can see the kingdom of God unless they are born again, of water and the Spirit. In this sub-strand you will retell that meeting, learn about repentance and baptism, and recite John 3:16.

## Strand 3.0: The Life of Jesus Christ
Sub-strand 3.9: Nicodemus’ encounter with Jesus Christ
Suggested lessons: 3

## Source
• KICD Grade 4 Christian Religious Education Curriculum Design (Revised 2024) — Strand 3.0 The Life of Jesus Christ, Sub-strand 3.9 Nicodemus' encounter with Jesus Christ
• John 3:1-5; John 3:16

PAGE 2: Learning outcomes

## Learning outcomes
By the end of the sub-strand, the learner should be able to:
a) retell the story of Nicodemus’ encounter with Jesus Christ
b) acknowledge that repentance of sins draws us close to Christ
c) discuss the importance of baptism to Christians today
d) recite John 3:16 and believe in Jesus Christ to inherit eternal life

## Key inquiry questions
1. How did Nicodemus’ encounter with Jesus Christ change his life?

PAGE 3: How we will learn

## Learning experiences
• read John 3:1-5 and say how they respond to Christ’s saving grace
• role-play the story of Nicodemus’ encounter with Jesus Christ
• discuss how repentance of sins can draw them to Christ
• watch a video on Nicodemus’ conversion
• say why baptism is important to Christians today
• sing a song on Nicodemus’ conversion
• tell how they respond to John 3:16

## Core competencies
• Communication: speaking skills are portrayed as learners read the Bible and tell how they respond to Christ’s saving grace.
• Learning to learn: the skill of working collaboratively is enhanced as learners discuss how repentance of sins can draw them to Christ.

## Values
• Respect: learners display humility as they role-play the story of Nicodemus.

## Pertinent and contemporary issues
• Social Cohesion: learners demonstrate teamwork while carrying out various activities.

## Links to other learning areas
• English: speaking skills are enhanced as learners speak fluently and confidently.
• Creative Arts: creative skills are applied as learners role-play and sing a song on Nicodemus’ conversion.

PAGE 4: Lesson 1: Nicodemus comes to Jesus at night

LESSON 1: NICODEMUS COMES TO JESUS AT NIGHT
===========================================

## What you will learn
• Retell John 3:1-5.
• Explain what Jesus meant by being born again in this passage.

Curriculum outcomes: a) retell the story of Nicodemus’ encounter with Jesus Christ

## Introduction
Some people come to Jesus with questions they do not want a crowd to hear. Nicodemus came at night. Jesus answered him with a truth about a new beginning.

PAGE 5: Lesson 1: Nicodemus comes to Jesus at night — Notes 1

## Notes

Read John 3:1-5 and retell only that conversation.

Nicodemus was a Pharisee and a member of the Jewish ruling council. He came to Jesus at night and said, "Rabbi, we know that you are a teacher who has come from God. For no one could perform the signs you are doing if God were not with him."

Jesus replied, "Very truly I tell you, no one can see the kingdom of God unless they are born again."

Nicodemus asked, "How can someone be born when they are old? Surely they cannot enter a second time into their mother's womb to be born!"

Jesus answered, "Very truly I tell you, no one can enter the kingdom of God unless they are born of water and the Spirit."

PAGE 6: Lesson 1: Nicodemus comes to Jesus at night — What the words mean

### What the words mean
A Pharisee was a Jewish teacher who was careful about the law. The ruling council was the group of leaders. Rabbi means teacher. Signs are the mighty works Jesus was doing, which showed Nicodemus that God was with Him.

Born again does not mean a second birth from a mother, which is what Nicodemus thought. Jesus corrected him. It means a new life from God. Verse 5 says this new birth is of water and the Spirit. Without it, a person cannot see or enter the kingdom of God.

PAGE 7: Lesson 1: Nicodemus comes to Jesus at night — Notes 3

The passage shows Nicodemus respectful and puzzled. He already called Jesus a teacher come from God. Jesus told him he needed more than respect. He needed to be born again. Do not add later scenes that these verses do not contain. Role-play the night visit, the praise, the saying about being born again, Nicodemus' question, and Jesus' answer about water and the Spirit.

## Key words
• Pharisee — a Jewish teacher careful about God's law; Nicodemus was one
• born again — the new life from God that Jesus said a person needs in order to see the kingdom
• signs — the mighty works of Jesus that showed God was with Him

PAGE 8: Lesson 1: Nicodemus comes to Jesus at night — Role-play the night conversation

## Activity: Role-play the night conversation
You will need: Bible, Space to act

1. Read John 3:1-5.

2. Role-play Nicodemus' encounter with Jesus: the night visit, the words about signs, and the teaching about being born again.

3. Say how a person can respond to Christ's saving grace: by listening, repenting and believing.

4. If a video on Nicodemus is available, watch it and check which parts match John 3:1-5.

PAGE 9: Lesson 1: Nicodemus comes to Jesus at night — Answers to practice

## Practice

1. Who was Nicodemus, and when did he come to Jesus?

2. What did he say about Jesus?

3. What did Jesus say a person must be, to see and enter the kingdom of God?

## Answers to practice

1. He was a Pharisee and a member of the Jewish ruling council. He came at night.

2. He called Him Rabbi and said Jesus was a teacher come from God, because no one could do those signs unless God was with Him.

3. Born again, of water and the Spirit.

PAGE 10: Lesson 2: Repentance draws us close to Christ

## Summary
• Nicodemus came to Jesus at night and said God was with Him.
• Jesus said no one can see the kingdom unless they are born again.
• That new birth is of water and the Spirit, not a return to a mother's womb.

LESSON 2: REPENTANCE DRAWS US CLOSE TO CHRIST
=============================================

## What you will learn
• Explain how repentance of sins draws a person close to Christ.
• Say how he or she will respond to Christ's saving grace.

Curriculum outcomes: b) acknowledge that repentance of sins draws us close to Christ

## Introduction
Nicodemus was an important teacher, but Jesus still spoke to him about a new birth. Being close to Christ is not a matter of a high position. It begins when a person turns from sin.

PAGE 11: Lesson 2: Repentance draws us close to Christ — How repentance draws us close

## Notes

Repentance means turning away from sin and turning to God. Jesus told Nicodemus that entry into the kingdom needs a new birth. A person who loves sin and will not turn is not drawing near. A person who repents is answering the call to be born again.

### How repentance draws us close
- We admit that we have done wrong. Pride keeps us far away.
- We ask Jesus for forgiveness.
- We stop the wrong action: lying, stealing, cruelty, impure talk.
- We start the right action: truth, kindness, prayer, obedience.
- We come to Him even if, like Nicodemus, we still have questions. He receives people who come honestly.

Saving grace is the kindness of Christ that saves people who do not deserve it. Nicodemus had learnt that the signs showed God was with Jesus. Responding to that grace means more than noticing the signs. It means trusting Jesus and turning from sin.

PAGE 12: Lesson 2: Repentance draws us close to Christ — Notes 3

Discuss this in a group. One learner may say, "I will stop cheating and ask God to forgive me." Another may say, "I will pray every night and obey my parents." Those are real responses. Humility belongs here. Nicodemus, a leader, still had to be taught. Role-play him listening, not arguing to win. Respect is shown when we let Jesus' words correct us.

You can be young and still repent. Age was Nicodemus' puzzle, not a barrier Jesus accepted. "How can someone be born when they are old?" Jesus answered with God's work: water and the Spirit. Whether a person is old or in Grade 4, the way near to Christ is repentance and trust.

PAGE 13: Lesson 2: Repentance draws us close to Christ — Discuss repentance

## Key words
• repentance — turning away from sin and turning to God
• grace — God's kindness that saves, which we do not earn
• humility — a modest heart that is willing to be taught

## Activity: Discuss repentance
You will need: Bible, Exercise book

1. Discuss how repentance of sins can draw you to Christ.

2. Each learner says one way he or she will respond to Christ's saving grace.

3. Role-play Nicodemus listening humbly to Jesus.

4. Write a one-sentence prayer of repentance.

PAGE 14: Lesson 2: Repentance draws us close to Christ — Answers to practice

## Practice

1. What is repentance?

2. Why was Nicodemus' high position not enough?

3. Give two ways to respond to Christ's saving grace.

## Answers to practice

1. Turning away from sin and turning to God.

2. Jesus said no one can see the kingdom of God unless they are born again.

3. Any two: admit sin, ask for forgiveness, stop a wrong action, obey, pray, believe in Jesus.

## Summary
• Repentance turns a person from sin to Christ.
• A high position cannot replace the new birth.
• We respond to Christ's grace by believing, repenting and obeying.

PAGE 15: Lesson 3: Baptism and John 3:16

LESSON 3: BAPTISM AND JOHN 3:16
===============================

## What you will learn
• Discuss the importance of baptism to Christians today.
• Recite John 3:16 and say what it means to believe in Jesus.

Curriculum outcomes: c) discuss the importance of baptism to Christians today; d) recite John 3:16 and believe in Jesus Christ to inherit eternal life

## Introduction
Jesus told Nicodemus that the new birth is of water and the Spirit. Christians connect this teaching with baptism and with faith. John 3:16 tells why believing in Jesus matters.

PAGE 16: Lesson 3: Baptism and John 3:16 — Notes 2

## Notes

### Baptism
Baptism is the Christian act of being baptised with water in the name of Jesus. In John 3:5 Jesus says no one can enter the kingdom of God unless they are born of water and the Spirit. Christians today take baptism seriously because Jesus joined water and the Spirit with entering the kingdom.

Baptism is important because:

- Jesus taught that the new birth involves water and the Spirit.
- It shows that a person has turned from sin and belongs to Jesus.
- It is a beginning of a new life, which is what "born again" means.
- The church obeys this teaching and welcomes the baptised person.
- It is done in public, so the believer is not hiding faith.

PAGE 17: Lesson 3: Baptism and John 3:16 — Notes 3

Baptism is not a magic wash that leaves the heart unchanged. It belongs with repentance and belief. A learner prepares by listening to the Bible, talking with parents and church leaders, and turning from sin. Different churches baptise at different ages. Speak respectfully about the practice of your church, and remember the verse that unites Christians: new birth by water and the Spirit.

PAGE 18: Lesson 3: Baptism and John 3:16 — John 3:16

### John 3:16
Recite: "For God so loved the world that he gave his one and only Son, that whoever believes in him shall not perish but have eternal life."

God loved the world. He gave His Son. Whoever believes in Jesus will not perish but will have eternal life. Eternal life is life with God that death does not end. Believing means trusting Jesus, not merely knowing His name.

Tell how you respond to this verse: thank God for His love, believe in Jesus, repent, and follow Him. Sing a song about Nicodemus' meeting with Jesus and about God's love in John 3:16.

PAGE 19: Lesson 3: Baptism and John 3:16 — Recite John 3:16

## Key words
• baptism — the Christian act of being baptised with water, joined in John 3:5 with the new birth
• believe — to trust Jesus, not only to know His name
• eternal life — life with God that John 3:16 promises to whoever believes in Jesus

## Activity: Recite John 3:16
You will need: Bible, Flash cards

1. Say why baptism is important to Christians today, using John 3:5.

2. Write John 3:16 on a flash card and recite it.

3. Each learner tells how he or she responds to John 3:16.

4. Sing a song on Nicodemus' encounter with Jesus and on God's love.

## Practice

1. What does John 3:5 say is needed to enter the kingdom of God?

2. Give two reasons why baptism is important to Christians.

3. Recite John 3:16.

PAGE 20: Lesson 3: Baptism and John 3:16 — Answers to practice

## Answers to practice

1. To be born of water and the Spirit.

2. Any two: Jesus taught new birth of water and the Spirit; it shows we belong to Jesus; it marks a new life; it follows repentance and belief.

3. For God so loved the world that he gave his one and only Son, that whoever believes in him shall not perish but have eternal life.

## Summary
• Jesus said people must be born of water and the Spirit.
• Baptism is important because it belongs with that new birth, repentance and faith.
• John 3:16: God loved the world and gave His Son so that believers may have eternal life.

PAGE 21: Revision quiz

REVISION QUIZ
=============

Answer all the questions, then mark yourself on the Answers tab.

1. Nicodemus' conversation in this sub-strand is in:
   A. John 3:1-5
   B. Luke 15:8-10
   C. Luke 7:11-16
   D. Numbers 22:28

2. Nicodemus was...
   A. a fisherman from Galilee
   B. a Pharisee and a member of the Jewish ruling council
   C. a Roman tax collector
   D. the angel Gabriel

3. He came to Jesus...
   A. at night
   B. at noon in the market only
   C. during the feeding of a crowd, in this passage
   D. on a donkey

4. Nicodemus said Jesus was a teacher come from God because:
   A. of the signs Jesus did
   B. Jesus had paid him
   C. the crowd forced him
   D. he had read Genesis that morning

5. Jesus said no one can see the kingdom of God unless they are:
   A. rich
   B. born again
   C. a member of the council
   D. able to enter the womb a second time

6. Born of water and the Spirit means, in Jesus' answer:

7. Repentance draws a person close to Christ because:
   A. turning from sin is how we answer His call to a new life
   B. sin keeps us near Him
   C. leaders do not need to repent
   D. questions are forbidden

8. Baptism is important to Christians today because:
   A. Jesus said people must be born of water and the Spirit
   B. it replaces belief
   C. only Pharisees may be baptised
   D. John 3:5 forbids water

9. John 3:16 says God loved the world and gave:
   A. His one and only Son
   B. a silver coin
   C. a mustard seed only
   D. the city of Nain

10. Whoever believes in Jesus will...

PAGE 22: Quiz answers

ANSWERS
=======

1. A. John 3:1-5
   The class reads John 3:1-5.

2. B. a Pharisee and a member of the Jewish ruling council
   John 3:1 gives these two facts.

3. A. at night
   John 3:2 says he came at night.

4. A. of the signs Jesus did
   John 3:2 says no one could do those signs unless God was with Him.

5. B. born again
   John 3:3 says they must be born again.

6. The new birth God gives, which Nicodemus could not get by entering his mother's womb again.
   John 3:4-5 corrects Nicodemus' idea of a physical second birth.

7. A. turning from sin is how we answer His call to a new life
   Jesus required a new birth, so repentance and trust are the way near to Him.

8. A. Jesus said people must be born of water and the Spirit
   John 3:5 joins water and the Spirit with entering the kingdom.

9. A. His one and only Son
   The verse says God gave His one and only Son.

10. Not perish but have eternal life.
   That is the promise of John 3:16.

### Baptism
Baptism is the Christian act of being baptised with water in the name of Jesus. In John 3:5 Jesus says no one can enter the kingdom of God unless they are born of water and the Spirit. Christians today take baptism seriously because Jesus joined water and the Spirit with entering the kingdom.

Baptism is important because:

- Jesus taught that the new birth involves water and the Spirit.
- It shows that a person has turned from sin and belongs to Jesus.
- It is a beginning of a new life, which is what "born again" means.
- The church obeys this teaching and welcomes the baptised person.
- It is done in public, so the believer is not hiding faith.

studyPages.title: Lesson 3: Baptism and John 3:16 — Notes 3
studyPages.body: Baptism is not a magic wash that leaves the heart unchanged. It belongs with repentance and belief. A learner prepares by listening to the Bible, talking with parents and church leaders, and turning from sin. Different churches baptise at different ages. Speak respectfully about the practice of your church, and remember the verse that unites Christians: new birth by water and the Spirit.

studyPages.title: Lesson 3: Baptism and John 3:16 — John 3:16
studyPages.body:
### John 3:16
Recite: "For God so loved the world that he gave his one and only Son, that whoever believes in him shall not perish but have eternal life."

God loved the world. He gave His Son. Whoever believes in Jesus will not perish but will have eternal life. Eternal life is life with God that death does not end. Believing means trusting Jesus, not merely knowing His name.

Tell how you respond to this verse: thank God for His love, believe in Jesus, repent, and follow Him. Sing a song about Nicodemus' meeting with Jesus and about God's love in John 3:16.

studyPages.title: Lesson 3: Baptism and John 3:16 — Recite John 3:16
studyPages.body:
## Key words
• baptism — the Christian act of being baptised with water, joined in John 3:5 with the new birth
• believe — to trust Jesus, not only to know His name
• eternal life — life with God that John 3:16 promises to whoever believes in Jesus

## Activity: Recite John 3:16
You will need: Bible, Flash cards

1. Say why baptism is important to Christians today, using John 3:5.

2. Write John 3:16 on a flash card and recite it.

3. Each learner tells how he or she responds to John 3:16.

4. Sing a song on Nicodemus' encounter with Jesus and on God's love.

## Practice

1. What does John 3:5 say is needed to enter the kingdom of God?

2. Give two reasons why baptism is important to Christians.

3. Recite John 3:16.

studyPages.title: Lesson 3: Baptism and John 3:16 — Answers to practice
studyPages.body:
## Answers to practice

1. To be born of water and the Spirit.

2. Any two: Jesus taught new birth of water and the Spirit; it shows we belong to Jesus; it marks a new life; it follows repentance and belief.

3. For God so loved the world that he gave his one and only Son, that whoever believes in him shall not perish but have eternal life.

## Summary
• Jesus said people must be born of water and the Spirit.
• Baptism is important because it belongs with that new birth, repentance and faith.
• John 3:16: God loved the world and gave His Son so that believers may have eternal life.

studyPages.title: Revision quiz
studyPages.body:
REVISION QUIZ
=============

Answer all the questions, then mark yourself on the Answers tab.

1. Nicodemus' conversation in this sub-strand is in:
   A. John 3:1-5
   B. Luke 15:8-10
   C. Luke 7:11-16
   D. Numbers 22:28

2. Nicodemus was...
   A. a fisherman from Galilee
   B. a Pharisee and a member of the Jewish ruling council
   C. a Roman tax collector
   D. the angel Gabriel

3. He came to Jesus...
   A. at night
   B. at noon in the market only
   C. during the feeding of a crowd, in this passage
   D. on a donkey

4. Nicodemus said Jesus was a teacher come from God because:
   A. of the signs Jesus did
   B. Jesus had paid him
   C. the crowd forced him
   D. he had read Genesis that morning

5. Jesus said no one can see the kingdom of God unless they are:
   A. rich
   B. born again
   C. a member of the council
   D. able to enter the womb a second time

6. Born of water and the Spirit means, in Jesus' answer:

7. Repentance draws a person close to Christ because:
   A. turning from sin is how we answer His call to a new life
   B. sin keeps us near Him
   C. leaders do not need to repent
   D. questions are forbidden

8. Baptism is important to Christians today because:
   A. Jesus said people must be born of water and the Spirit
   B. it replaces belief
   C. only Pharisees may be baptised
   D. John 3:5 forbids water

9. John 3:16 says God loved the world and gave:
   A. His one and only Son
   B. a silver coin
   C. a mustard seed only
   D. the city of Nain

10. Whoever believes in Jesus will...

studyPages.title: Quiz answers
studyPages.body:
ANSWERS
=======

1. A. John 3:1-5
   The class reads John 3:1-5.

2. B. a Pharisee and a member of the Jewish ruling council
   John 3:1 gives these two facts.

3. A. at night
   John 3:2 says he came at night.

4. A. of the signs Jesus did
   John 3:2 says no one could do those signs unless God was with Him.

5. B. born again
   John 3:3 says they must be born again.

6. The new birth God gives, which Nicodemus could not get by entering his mother's womb again.
   John 3:4-5 corrects Nicodemus' idea of a physical second birth.

7. A. turning from sin is how we answer His call to a new life
   Jesus required a new birth, so repentance and trust are the way near to Him.

8. A. Jesus said people must be born of water and the Spirit
   John 3:5 joins water and the Spirit with entering the kingdom.

9. A. His one and only Son
   The verse says God gave His one and only Son.

10. Not perish but have eternal life.
   That is the promise of John 3:16.
